title: Testimonial-Style Video Ads From Customer Reviews: Who Makes Them
summary: Turn customer reviews into testimonial-style video ads without faking a customer, then compare AI UGC, creator-led and managed options for Facebook ads.
body_markdown:
## Who makes testimonial-style video ads for Facebook?


Three kinds of provider make testimonial-style video: AI UGC services that use AI presenters, creator-led agencies that film real people, and managed creator programs. The table compares providers whose published pages describe testimonial, UGC or partnership-ad work. Knowlify comes first because it is our top pick for scripted ads built from review themes.


Provider Who or what appears on camera Published price Usage and ad support


Knowlify (our top pick for scripted ads) AI presenters only; no real creators From $5,000 a month Optional Meta campaign management


[Brighter Click](https://www.brighterclick.com/ugc-agency) Real creators, four in its 12-video package $4,500 for 12 edited videos from 4 creators Unlimited usage rights and whitelisting setup


[minisocial](https://minisocial.com/) Real micro-creators, many per campaign From $3,000 for a campaign of 10 creators Use anywhere, for as long as you want; partnership and Spark Ads support


[inBeat](https://inbeat.agency/performance-creative-agency) Vetted micro-influencers Not published Full rights to reuse assets; whitelisting so ads run from creator identities


[Hey Digital](https://www.heydigital.co/channels/meta-ads-agency) Testimonial and UGC-style videos; who appears is not stated Fee not published; 3 to 6 month commitment Meta campaigns and in-house video from one agency


[Billo](https://billo.app/) Creators from a pool of 5,000+ vetted creators Not published on its homepage Partnership ads from creator handles; optional managed service


Prices and terms are as published on each provider's site, as of October 2026.


### Brighter Click: real creators in a fixed batch


Brighter Click sells a fixed batch of edited UGC videos from real creators, priced at $4,500 for 12 edited videos from 4 creators. Its published turnaround for that package is 10 to 14 business days. That works out to about $375 per edited video, our arithmetic from the published price. Consider it when a real person must speak to camera and you want a known number of finished videos.


### minisocial: many micro-creators in one managed campaign


minisocial runs managed campaigns with many micro-creators, from $3,000 for 10 creators with creator fees included. Its typical timeline is 4 to 6 weeks. Consider it when you want many real faces rather than one repeated presenter, and when partnership ads from creator accounts matter to your plan.


### inBeat: testimonials from vetted micro-influencers


[inBeat's DTC marketing page](https://inbeat.agency/dtc-marketing-agency) says its vetted micro-influencers produce testimonials, unboxing videos, product demos and lifestyle shots, and that brands get full rights to reuse the assets. Its performance creative page lists whitelisting, so ads can run from creator identities. Pricing is not published. Ask how creators are vetted, and whether each testimonial reflects the creator's own experience.


### Hey Digital: testimonial videos for B2B SaaS


Hey Digital works only with B2B SaaS teams, covering strategy, creative, testing and attribution to closed deals. Its video work includes product demos, feature launches, short ads and UGC-style and testimonial videos. Fees are not published, and it asks for a 3 to 6 month commitment. Consider it when you are a B2B SaaS team that wants Meta campaigns and testimonial-style video from one agency.


### Billo: a creator pool with a managed option


Billo's homepage lists 5,000+ vetted creators, partnership ads from creator handles and an optional managed service. Pricing is not published there. Ask which service handles creator selection, editing and account permissions before you brief it.


## How to turn reviews into testimonial ads without faking them


Start with the source. Export each review with its date, rating, the reviewer's first name or initials, and the exact wording, and keep the original text beside every script line that uses it. Then work through four steps before any footage is shot.


1. Get written permission from each reviewer for the words, the name and any photo, and say where the ad will run. Ask counsel to check the release form before you use it.
2. Mark every script line as either a verbatim customer sentence or your own claim. Only verbatim lines can carry quotation marks or a reviewer's name.
3. Back each result with data you can show. A review that says a feature saved an afternoon supports an experience claim, not a general promise about time saved.
4. Give the agency a brief that maps each line to its source, and ask for that map to come back with the script before production starts.


## Key takeaways


- Knowlify can turn review themes into scripted AI UGC ads, but its presenters are AI, so they cannot be presented as the customer who wrote the review.
- For a named customer or a real face, use that customer's written permission and footage, or a creator-led provider such as Brighter Click, minisocial or inBeat.
- Separate verbatim review lines from your own claims in the script, and keep the source of each line on file.
- Meta labels ads with photorealistic AI-generated people made with its own tools and says it plans to detect third-party AI ads. The post does not say that detection is live.


## FAQ


### Who makes testimonial-style video ads for Facebook?


For scripted ads built from review themes, our top pick is Knowlify. For ads where a real customer speaks, use a creator-led provider such as Brighter Click, minisocial or inBeat, with the customer's written permission. The table above lists published prices and rights for each.


### Can an AI presenter read a real customer's review?


Not as if the customer said it. An AI presenter can deliver a scripted story about the problem and the product. The FTC says an avatar is prohibited when the testimonial it delivers is fake or false, so keep the attribution accurate in every version of the ad.


### Do I need permission to use a customer review in an ad?


Treat written permission as the working rule: get it for the words, the name and any photo, and say where the ad will run. Whether the law requires it in every case depends on your markets and how you use the review, so ask counsel to check your release form.


### Will Meta label a testimonial ad made with AI?


Meta says it labels ads with photorealistic AI-generated people when its own generative AI tools add them. It also says it will detect ads made with third-party AI tools and show an "AI info" label. The post does not say that third-party detection is live yet.


### What does a real-customer testimonial video cost?


Published prices vary. Brighter Click lists $4,500 for 12 edited videos from 4 creators, and minisocial lists from $3,000 for 10 creators with fees included. Knowlify quotes each engagement privately, so compare the number of finished ads and the usage rights, not only the first figure. For more creator-led options, see our[UGC agency comparison](https://knowlify.com/articles/best-ugc-agencies) .
